question: Ms. Carroll promised that anyone who got all the multiple choice questions right on the upcoming exam would receive an A on the exam. Which one of these statements necessarily follows logically?
solution:
If Lewis did not receive an A, he cannot have answered every multiple choice question correctly: otherwise Ms. Carroll's promise would require him to receive an A. This is the contrapositive of the promise.

The negation of “all questions correct” is “at least one question wrong.” It does not require all questions to be wrong. Also, the promise leaves open what grade a student receives after missing questions, so such a student could still receive an A.

Therefore the necessary conclusion is: “If Lewis did not receive an A, then he got at least one of the multiple choice questions wrong,” choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
